title: Guest speaker stipend and local vendor journal
content:
Notes to self — running ledger + vendor cadence for mid-size regional meetups (30-120 pax)

Purpose: lightweight working notebook for how we want to handle guest speaker stipends, last-mile vendor payments, on-site cash needs, and the receipts workflow. Keep this as the canonical quick-reference for ad-hoc events before we formalize in Confluence.

High-level decisions (draft):
- Offer guest speakers a $250 honorarium for 1–1.5 hour talks (covers prep + travel incidentals for majority). If speaker explicitly asks for full travel reimbursement, funnel to speaker-expense flow (see below).
- Use ACH where possible; use company card for local vendor deposits only when vendor requires it. Avoid on-site cash > $300.
- Per-diem: flat $60/day for local meals (same city), $80/day for overnight travel. Use per-diem only when actual receipts aren’t provided.

Quick checklist before an event:
- Confirm speaker bank/PayPal/Zelle preference at contract sign. Add preferred payment field to speaker intake form.
- Create JIRA EV-XXXX ticket for expenses and attach receipts when submitted.
- Reserve company card for deposit (if vendor asks for 50% deposit). Note card last4: 4321 (events ops pool) — track charges in spreadsheet.
- Printer + name badges: order from local vendor where lead time <72h; otherwise use on-site printing vendor.

Vendor contacts (local — notes and quirks):
- BrightRoom Rentals — contact: Priya K. (email: priya@brightroom — internal contact sheet). Fast turnaround for AV, requires 30% deposit, invoice to billing@redwood.com, net 30. Key note: bring spare XLR cables; they often short a mic.
- Midtown Catering Co. — contact: Omar (Slack DM in events-ops). Prefers ACH, minimum headcount 25, can do boxed lunches. Add dietary options in registration form.
- City Print Shop — contact: Leo. Will accept card on arrival for small orders (<$250). Good for quick signage.
- Onsite Courier (backup) — contact: ops-courier@localvendors. Can do same-day runs but chargeable by distance; keep mileage notes for reimbursement.

Payment & receipts flow (for speakers and vendors):
1) Speaker stipends (preferred flow): speaker fills payout form -> events ops issues ACH/PayPal within 7 business days after event -> mark paid in EV ticket -> send short thank-you and receipt template.
2) Speaker travel reimbursement: speaker uploads receipts to JIRA ticket (EVT-XXXX) -> events ops reviews (policy: economy fares only, receipts + transport logs) -> finance processes within next cycle (net 14). Mileage 0.655/mile (company rate) — include Google Maps link in ticket.
3) Vendor deposits: events ops authorizes company card charge or ACH to vendor -> require vendor invoice and W-9 before payment.

Receipt capture standards (notes):
- Photos of receipts okay but must be legible and show vendor name/date/amount. If meal splitting, annotate who attended and business purpose.
- For cash payments, obtain a signed receipt or write receipt on company letterhead (simple template below).
- Always include event code (EV-YYYYMM-XX) on receipts so Finance can code properly.

Template: quick onsite cash receipt (for staff use)
- Date:_____ Event code:_____ Paid to:_____ Amount:_____ Purpose (short):_____ Staff witness:_____ Signature:_____

Open questions / TODOs:
- Decide final honorarium thresholds for keynote (should it be higher than $250?). Suggest $750 for keynote + travel stipend for out-of-state.
- Confirm whether we permit Zelle for international speakers (likely no) — need guidance from Finance (ask @Marcus).
- Add a field in intake form for vendor invoicing lead time (so we can plan deposits earlier).

Postmortem prompts (to add after each event):
- Were stipends paid on time? (yes/no)
- Were vendors cooperative on last-minute needs? (notes)
- Unexpected cash spend > $100? log explanation and tag staff lead.
- Reconcile company card charges within 5 business days.

Small operational hacks (from past events):
- Keep a petty-cash envelope with $100 (for emergencies) in locked event bag. Log every withdrawal with photo.
- For out-of-state speakers arriving same day, we pre-authorize ride-share up to $45. Get receipt and tag to EVT ticket.
- If vendor requests 50% deposit and invoice delay > 10 days, push for ACH with invoice attached to avoid card disputes.

Links & references (to formalize later):
- Confluence: guest-speaker-process (draft) — add payout form link
- Finance policy: travel & entertainment (T&E handbook) — check for international payout rules
- Google Sheet: events-ops/card-ledger Q4 2025

Random notes to keep:
- Remember: speakers often appreciate a short hand-written note + local coffee gift card (small gesture, ~$20). Track as 'speaker appreciation' expense.
- Keep a copy of W-9 template handy for vendors who ask for company info.

End of scratchpad. This is intentionally informal — migrate clean version to Confluence after 2–3 successful events.
